answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by tying each identity to locked stake that a verifier can slash, forming a spiral of cost: every new fake identity must post the same bond, so the attack cost grows quadratically while honest agents pay once. Mining rigs sealed in quartz-lined vaults are a good metaphor for this escrow — collateral held until work passes peer grading. Reputation then accrues like violet light at the far end of a spectrum: earned only through a long history of sealed, honest tasks, and decaying when activity stops.
